title: The Page Who Understood the Speech of Birds

keywords: the page who feigned to know the speech of birds
full_text:
A wealthy King of Persia had in his service a clever young page named Farhad, who noticed that the king had neglected the repair of the frontier fortresses, spending his treasury exclusively on banquets while the city walls fell into dangerous disrepair.

One morning, while the king was strolling through the palace gardens, two swallows began chattering loudly upon the cornice of a crumbling pavilion.

The king smiled and asked jokingly: 'Farhad, you claim to be educated in many subtle arts; can you tell me what those two swallows are debating with such furious chatter?'

Farhad bowed with grave solemnity and answered: 'Sire, the swallows are arranging a wedding between their fledglings. The father of the bride says: "I will consent to the union on condition that you grant my daughter forty ruined towers in the frontier walls for her nesting places!" And the father of the groom replies: "Rejoice! If our gracious King continues to neglect his masonry for another two seasons, I shall easily grant you a hundred ruined fortresses!"'

The king was struck dumb by the page’s brilliant allegory. He realized that while he feasted, the defenses of his realm were becoming nesting grounds for swallows.

The king laughed heartily, commended Farhad for his witty tact, and immediately ordered the repair of every fortress across the frontier, learning that true loyalty uses wit to remind power of its duties.
moral: Tactful allegory and witty parables can awaken a ruler to civic duty without provoking offense.
